title: Made a Road Rash x DiRT mashup in about 3 days with AI. The dirt bike is still a mess
author: titkun
selftext:
I’ve been making games for about 25 years (mostly AAA and now indie) and wanted to see how far I could get in a few days with AI doing a lot of the heavy lifting. I wanted to do something like Road Rash (the 1991 version, I'm that old) and a cool rally game like Dirt. 

The result is Rally Road Rash: 4 vehicles, 5 dirt stages, drift boost, jump pads and I replace the chains with rockets.

Opus 5.5 did most of the vehicles and physics. For the look, I gave Astra 6 a screenshot of a benchmark visual and told it to get to at least 90% of that quality. It ran for 3 to 4 hours on most of the maps. I tweaked the levels by hand in our editor. The music comes from Sandscape and ElevenLabs, and Sandscape handles the multiplayer and leaderboards, so I never touched that part.

The dirt bike is where it fell apart. I thought it would be the most fun of the four and it ended up being the jankiest. I’m still iterating on it and hope to get it right in the next pass.

Full disclosure: I’m one of the people building Sandscape, so take that into account. If anyone here has fought with bike physics before, I’d love to hear how you handled it.

comments.author: kb23100
comments.body: are the models done in blender via mcp or generated by opus

replies.author: titkun
replies.body: It’s a mix of Sandscape, Meshy and Opus. The vehicles and main props come from Meshy and the simpler background meshes are basic geometry that Opus generated in code via our tool. Everything gets assembled and tweaked in Sandscape
